rationale: I read the full canonical original, exact approved specification, live and frozen targets, shared NMFDecision helper and full finite-machine/encoding/verifier definitions, and final implementation notes. ORIGINAL is byte-identical and both independent preimplementation approval bindings are intact. No catalog truth proof is inferred from the prior resolved status.

Input contains arbitrary rational rectangular data and rational threshold; ValidInput imposes only entrywise and threshold nonnegativity. MathematicalYes quantifies genuine real m-by-2 and 2-by-n factors with every entry nonnegative, the literal complete double Frobenius sum and the non-strict threshold comparison. Zero entries, zero factors, inner rank below two and exact equality are included; there is no rational-witness, exact-rank, symmetry, positivity or spectral promise.

Natural dimensions include every positive rectangular format and the explicitly disclosed empty-format extension. Empty sums have zero error and nonnegative thresholds accept these trivial cases, without excluding any original instance or adding an invertibility/minimum-size restriction.

Encode writes both canonical framed natural dimensions, every rational coefficient by nested List.ofFn in increasing row-major order, and the rational threshold. The two dimensions determine every coefficient position; signed reduced numerators and positive denominators retain exact input data and all binary bits. It is the concrete shared grammar, not an arbitrary encoder or unit-cost rational size measure.

DecisionLanguage is the fixed ordinary set of encoded valid instances having the exact real factor property. Other words are negative by the approved ordinary-language convention. Every reduction and the separate P question use exactly this same language; no abstract predicate or output interpretation may be supplied by a reduction.

Complexity.InNP uses one finite verifier with uniformly polynomial certificate length and actual bounded acceptance on a fixed pair encoding. The verifier must return a Boolean on all encoded pairs, including overlong certificates. FiniteMachine has an actual finite TM0 transition table, current-symbol move/write operations, bounded iteration from the explicit input, reached terminality and exact full suffix output. These concrete imported meanings were rechecked.

Target expands ManyOneNPHard: every language in that NP class has a finite transducer and one polynomial bound fixed before every source word, with an actual terminating output and exact membership equivalence. No promise oracle, selected satisfiability equivalence, free reduction function or assumed runtime replaces ordinary polynomial many-one reduction. The original classification request is answered by the credited NP-hardness proposition without assuming the alternatives exhaust complexity possibilities.

PolynomialSolvability separately states InP for this same language. Its negation, NP membership, NP completeness, strong hardness and approximation-ratio hardness are not asserted. NP-hardness is therefore not silently turned into a P unequal to NP claim.

The shared NMFDecision owns the nominal Input type and unchanged encoder/mathematical language; live and frozen boundaries define their own closed Target and PolynomialSolvability over that same explicitly reviewed type. Full source closure/pin binding covers this shared meaning, so an rfl identity cannot by itself authorize semantic drift.

I independently compiled fresh Infrastructure, FiniteMachine, BinaryEncoding, Complexity, NMFDecision, live NM03, frozen NM03 and actual identities for BOTH Target and PolynomialSolvability into a separate macOS build. Every step exited0. Both named proposition closures show only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and their #assert_statement/#assert_trust kernel checks passed. General codec/model equivalence theorems, NP source completeness, concrete reductions and their complexity/error proofs remain future proof work rather than assumed target axioms.
verification_scope: Independent exact source/mathematical boundary review and fresh local kernel/frozen equality of both exported Props; no target proof or Linux result.
